the-ke-hrms.title: THE KE HRMS
the-ke-hrms.subtitle: WORKFORCE MANAGEMENT
the-ke-hrms.overview: An internal tool built to manage outsourced contractors, project staffing, performance evaluations, and tech stacks. I took the project from scratch to on-prem deployment, setting up a 3-tier permission model, 10+ protected routes, and a 7-step PostgreSQL migration pipeline.
keyFeatures: Role-based access (admin, sales support, sales rep) handled via JWT and HttpOnly cookies
Dashboard with RPC-backed metrics, contractor cards, and grade filters
Spreadsheet bulk imports and audit trail tracking for changes
Document and profile file management backed by a re-authentication flow (SecureDeleteModal)
myContributions: Designed the data schema and core system architecture for workers, assignments, and access roles
Built the frontend with Next.js 16 App Router, implementing route proxies and API-level permission checks
Wrote the auth flow (JWT + HttpOnly cookies), database migrations, RPC functions, and audit logging
Configured our internal Windows Server 2022 instance, setting up Gitea Actions and PM2 for automated rollouts
the-ke-hrms.challenges: Deploying onto on-prem Windows Server 2022 was the steepest curve. I had little background with Windows firewall rules or OS-specific service management, and wiring Gitea Actions to trigger zero-downtime PM2 restarts took several rounds of PowerShell script debugging.
the-ke-hrms.reflection: This was my first project where I owned everything end-to-end, including on-prem infrastructure. Dealing with strict database row-level security and deployment quirks made me much more comfortable making foundational architecture decisions.

haimdall-v3.title: Haimdall v3
haimdall-v3.subtitle: CARBON CREDIT MANAGEMENT
haimdall-v3.overview: A web platform built to track and manage carbon credits for sustainable agriculture. It renders and monitors 20,000+ farmland plots in real time alongside booking workflows and 5-language localization. I was the sole frontend engineer on the team.
keyFeatures: Interactive map rendering 20,000+ farmland polygons via deck.gl
Geospatial data dashboard with live field status updates
Full localization into 5 languages using next-intl (EN, KR, VI, KM, BN)
Dedicated modules for farmland verification, carbon metrics, and booking
myContributions: Built the entire frontend from scratch and set up the client-side architecture
Cut map initial load times by ~40% by adopting Mapbox Vector Tiles (MVT) and client-side caching
Set up role-based access control on top of Firebase Auth
Turned Figma specs into modular UI components for land tracking and reservation workflows
haimdall-v3.challenges: The map lagged severely whenever users panned across dense clusters of 20,000+ polygons. Transitioning from raw GeoJSON to Mapbox Vector Tiles (MVT) with deck.gl and setting up local caching resolved the bottleneck. Supporting non-Latin scripts like Khmer and Bengali also caused unexpected font flashes and layout breaks that required custom CSS fallbacks.
haimdall-v3.reflection: Handling that much geospatial data forced me to profile rendering performance systematically instead of just guessing. It also sharpened how I negotiate technical tradeoffs directly with backend engineers and designers.

independent-Journalist.title: Independent Journalist
independent-Journalist.subtitle: CUSTOM WORDPRESS WEBSITE
independent-Journalist.overview: A volunteer WordPress directory built to highlight independent YouTube reporters across the globe. It categorizes channels by region and topic, embedding direct links and donation QR codes while keeping page weight minimal without heavy plugins.
keyFeatures: Lightweight responsive card grid built for fast mobile browsing
Instant client-side search and category filtering with vanilla JavaScript
Dynamic channel cards with integrated donation QR codes and external links
9 custom page templates built without bloated third-party page builders
myContributions: Coded responsive page templates using Gutenberg blocks, custom HTML, and CSS
Wrote the search and filter logic in plain JavaScript to avoid external script overhead
Integrated QR code generation directly into the dynamic channel cards
Ran design review sessions directly with the organizer to iterate on layout and branding
independent-Journalist.challenges: We kicked off the project without any brand guidelines or wireframes. I drafted low-fidelity wireframes myself to align expectations with the client, then built custom templates so the site would stay fast instead of piling on third-party plugins.
independent-Journalist.reflection: Working with a non-technical client made me practice explaining technical constraints in plain terms. It also reinforced that vanilla code is often far more reliable and easier to maintain than a stack of WordPress plugins.

chezmari.title: Chez Mari Salon
chezmari.subtitle: WORDPRESS WEBSITE REDESIGN
chezmari.overview: A client redesign project for a local hair salon looking to modernize its brand. We built a responsive site with custom media galleries and an integrated appointment booking system that the owner could manage without technical help.
keyFeatures: Clean UI refresh aligned with the salon's existing brand identity
Custom WordPress dashboard tailored for quick staff and service updates
Self-service online booking system for appointments
Asynchronous image gallery with AJAX loading
myContributions: Managed sprint backlogs in Jira, coordinated Git branches, and led standups
Handled domain provisioning, DNS routing, SMTP setup, and production hosting
Implemented the media gallery page using AJAX to prevent page reloads
Customized the third-party booking plugin’s UI and deployed the final site
chezmari.challenges: The booking plugin’s markup was rigid and coupled tightly with its core logic. Restyling the booking flow without breaking internal date pickers and form submissions took careful DOM inspection. Translating why those technical limits existed to the salon owner was another challenge in itself.
chezmari.reflection: This project took me out of a pure code bubble into infrastructure setup, sprint management, and direct client communication. Our team took 1st place in the program evaluation.

Beep.title: Beep
Beep.subtitle: REACT NATIVE SAFETY APP
Beep.overview: A cross-platform mobile app that analyzes local crime data to assist with safer pedestrian navigation. It features route risk scoring, safe zone discovery, one-tap emergency SMS alerts, and community incident reports.
keyFeatures: Route guidance evaluated against public safety and crime datasets
Emergency SOS button broadcasting live coordinates via SMS
Pin-drop incident reporting with on-site photo attachments
Streamlined onboarding and user authentication flow
myContributions: Maintained repo workflows, Git branch conventions, and internal tech notes
Built the SOS trigger screen and wired audio alerts
Built the community incident logging flow with map-based photo pinning
Connected Firebase Realtime Database and automated SMS dispatch
Beep.challenges: Scope creep caused early confusion across the team, so we split project coordination into technical tasks and UI deliverables to realign responsibilities. On the code side, React Native and Expo were new to most of us, so getting background location tracking and SMS hooks to behave reliably took steady trial and error.
Beep.reflection: We had to pick up React Native and Expo from scratch while keeping up with a compressed schedule. Placing 3rd out of 10 teams validated that we were able to adapt and ship under pressure.

fourSeason.title: Four Season
fourSeason.subtitle: FULL-STACK BOOKING PLATFORM
fourSeason.overview: A full-stack booking system built for a Vancouver tour rental operator who was previously handling bookings manually via Instagram DMs. I built a web platform with live slot availability, automated confirmations, and a lightweight admin dashboard.
keyFeatures: Real-time tour slot calendar and booking engine
Automated customer confirmation emails via Resend API
Strapi CMS backend for straightforward non-technical schedule edits
Split architecture deployed on Vercel (frontend) and Render (backend)
myContributions: Shipped the entire application independently in 7 days
Designed the user flow and responsive UI from wireframe to code
Built the full-stack architecture using Next.js, Strapi, and PostgreSQL (Neon)
Set up transactional email triggers and configured production deployment pipelines
fourSeason.challenges: I hadn't integrated the Resend API before, so I had to work through the webhook and error handling docs quickly against a tight 7-day delivery window. Structuring Strapi’s permission policies with Neon PostgreSQL also required rigorous testing to prevent double-booking race conditions.
fourSeason.reflection: Taking a manual social media workflow and replacing it with a fully automated, deployed product in a single week proved I could ship a solid MVP fast without cutting corners on core UX.

hilton.title: Hilton
hilton.subtitle: HOTEL BOOKING APP REDESIGN
hilton.overview: A solo UI/UX and frontend redesign targeting friction points in the Hilton Honors mobile flow. I restructured the room selection, checkout, and digital check-in views, then rebuilt the core screens with a modular React component hierarchy.
keyFeatures: Streamlined room comparison and checkout funnel
Redesigned digital key and mobile check-in interface
Mobile-first responsive layouts styled with Tailwind CSS
Modular, reusable UI component library
myContributions: Mapped user drop-off points and layout clutter in the existing booking flow
Designed high-fidelity mockups focusing on mobile-first clarity
Built the interactive UI prototypes using clean, reusable React components
Fine-tuned responsive breakpoints to keep card views and modal sheets consistent across devices
hilton.challenges: The main friction was UX balance: simplifying the multi-step checkout without removing essential room metadata like cancellation policies or bed specs. Recreating flexible mobile drawer sheets and complex price breakdown cards in Tailwind without CSS bloat also took several refactors.
hilton.reflection: This gave me a chance to handle both the UX critique and the actual frontend implementation myself. Seeing firsthand how small design choices impact component state and CSS architecture made me a cleaner front-end engineer.
